questions.stem: What is the equation for kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is calculated using KE = 1/2 mv^2, where m is mass in kg and v is speed in m/s.

questions.stem: If the speed of an object is doubled, its kinetic energy will:
questions.explanation: Because speed is squared in KE = 1/2 mv^2, doubling the speed gives 2^2 = 4 times the kinetic energy.

questions.stem: Calculate the kinetic energy of a 2 kg ball moving at 10 m/s.
Why does doubling a car's speed quadruple its stopping distance (assuming constant braking force)?

options.text: Because the brakes are less effective at high speed
Because friction decreases at high speed
Because the car is heavier at higher speeds
Because kinetic energy depends on v^2, so the brakes must do four times as much work

questions.explanation: Since KE = 1/2 mv^2, doubling speed gives 4 times the kinetic energy. With constant braking force, 4 times the work (and therefore 4 times the distance) is needed to stop.

questions.stem: A 0.5 kg ball has 100 J of kinetic energy. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: v = sqrt(2 x KE / m) = sqrt(2 x 100 / 0.5) = sqrt(400) = 20 m/s.

questions.stem: Is kinetic energy a scalar or vector quantity?

options.text: Vector, because it can be negative
Scalar, because energy has no direction
Vector, because it depends on velocity

questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is a scalar quantity. Although velocity is a vector, kinetic energy uses speed squared and has no direction -- it is always positive or zero.

questions.stem: If the mass of a moving object is doubled while its speed stays the same, the kinetic energy will:
questions.explanation: KE = 1/2 mv^2. Kinetic energy is directly proportional to mass, so doubling the mass doubles the kinetic energy.
